items.text: **SC1.** When a fresh OpenCode session starts and the cwd is inside a canonical ADV worktree path (`~/.local/share/opencode/worktree/{40-hex}/change/{changeId}/`), the pane title shows the changeId shortly after init (subject to reachability).
**SC2.** When an agent actively works on a change cross-project (via `target_path`), the caller's pane title shows the target changeId.
**SC3.** Read/list/diagnostic/cleanup tool calls (same-project OR cross-project) do NOT touch the pane title.
**SC4.** The existing OSC title format policy (`rq-titleIdentity01` — `changeId`; `epicId | changeId`; no write when null) is preserved unchanged.

**AC1.** Given a fresh OpenCode session whose cwd matches `~/.local/share/opencode/worktree/{40-hex}/change/{changeId}/`, when the plugin initializes, the pane title is set to `{changeId}` if the change is reachable. If not reachable, no title write occurs (pane preserves prior state).
**AC2.** Given a fresh session whose cwd does NOT match the canonical worktree pattern, the plugin leaves the pointer null and writes no pane title at init.

**AC3.** Given a caller session with pointer=null and a `target_path` invocation of any `activeChangeRepointTools` tool (e.g. `adv_task_update`, `adv_run_test`, `adv_task_checkpoint`), when the target-project change is reachable, the caller's pane title is set to the target changeId.
**AC4.** Given a `target_path` invocation of any non-repoint ADV tool (e.g. `adv_change_show`, `adv_task_list`, `adv_status`), the caller's pane title is not touched.
**AC5.** Given the caller's pointer is set to a cross-project changeId X and `adv_change_close` or `adv_change_archive` succeeds for X (with or without target_path), the caller's pointer is cleared.
**AC6.** Given the caller's pointer is set to a cross-project changeId X and `adv_change_forget changeId:X` is invoked, the caller's pointer is cleared.
**AC7.** When the target-project reachability check fails for a `target_path` invocation, the tool call itself proceeds and returns its normal result; only the repoint is skipped.

**AC8.** Spec law `rq-activeChangePointer01` (parent requirement at `.adv/specs/advance-meta/spec.json:2765-2878` and `docs/specs/advance-meta.md`; specifically scenario `.7` at lines 2865-2877) text + scenario `.7` are revised to reflect: active-work cross-project calls repoint the caller's pointer to the target changeId; read/diagnostic calls do not; terminal transitions (close/archive/forget) clear regardless of project.
**AC9.** All existing scenarios for `rq-activeChangePointer01.1` through `.6` continue to pass without modification.
**AC10.** `pnpm test`, `pnpm run check`, and `pnpm run build` all succeed.

**C1.** ADR 0008 successor properties #6 (clean uninstall — no orphan pane titles after plugin disable) and #7 (crash safety — plugin crash does not wedge zellij-server) must be satisfied. The fix is in-process state; property #5 (≥16-session stress test) is N/A since no subprocess forks are introduced.
**C2.** `rq-titleIdentity01` (title format policy) must remain unchanged.
**C3.** `activeChangeRepointTools` allow-list (`plugin/src/index.ts:576-595`) must not be widened; it is already the correct narrow set of "actively working on the change" tools.
**C4.** Cross-project reachability check must NOT block the tool call itself on the target project's reachability failure — only the repoint is skipped.

**C5.** Cwd-detection must use the canonical ADV worktree path pattern (`~/.local/share/opencode/worktree/{40-hex}/change/{changeId}/`); non-canonical paths (random dirs named `change/foo/`) must not seed the pointer.
**C6.** Multi-session safety — concurrent OpenCode sessions on the same project must not corrupt each other's in-process pointer (already true; pointers are session-local).

**C7.** Reachability gate stays three-tier (Visibility → disk change.json → workflow state) per `rq-activeChangePointer01.5`; the cross-project path extends it to query the target project's tiers, not bypass it.
**C8.** Spec delta is a modify operation on `rq-activeChangePointer01.7`; no new spec requirement is introduced.
**DONT1.** No `opencode-zellij-status` server plugin revival or any equivalent per-event fork storm (ADR 0008 do-not-revive).
**DONT2.** No widening of the trigger surface beyond `activeChangeRepointTools` — including no repoint on read/list/diagnostic/cleanup/repair tool calls.
**DONT3.** No clearing or overwriting the pane title when no active change exists (`rq-titleIdentity01.2` — preserve last intentional title).
**DONT4.** No regression of the tmux code path.
**DONT5.** No new third-party dependency.
**DONT6.** No inference of changeId from non-canonical paths (random `~/dev/foo`, `~/scratch/change/bar`, etc.).
**DONT7.** No blocking of tool execution on target-project reachability failure — only the repoint is skipped.
**DONT8.** No per-event status cues (▶ ? ↻ ! ✓ emoji palette) — broader ADR 0008 successor backlog, separate work.
**DONT9.** No TAB title changes — the launcher owns those with project abbreviation.

documents.proposal:
# Fix zellij pane titles

## Why

The user observes zellij pane frames staying at default `Pane #1` during work on active changes — the visual coordination cue (which pane is working on which change) is missing. Two distinct scenarios produce this; both in scope per user clarification:

1. **Fresh session** — every OpenCode startup begins with pointer=null (no persistence since `index.ts:454-457` retired `handoff.json`). Until the first `activeChangeRepointTools` tool fires, pane stays at `Pane #1`.
2. **Cross-project (`target_path`) work** — `rq-activeChangePointer01.7` currently mandates that cross-project calls do not touch the caller's pointer. So a toolbox session driving an advance change (as this very session does) never shows the target changeId.

## Discovery root cause

**The OSC mechanism works** (live evidence: pane in tab `adv` shows `systemizeAdvOrchestration | addAdvMcpReadSurface` correctly). The bug is **contextual**: the OSC code path doesn't fire in scenarios 1 and 2 above.

The original triage hypothesis "silent TTY write failure" is **disproven**. The plugin's OSC writer (`events/terminal.ts:170-221`) reaches zellij's VTE parser when invoked.

## User decisions (Phase 4.5)

| Question | User's choice | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| Which scenario produces `Pane #1`? | Fresh session — never shows until restart | Scenario 1 in scope |
| How to detect active change at startup? | **Auto-detect from cwd** | Infer changeId from `change/<id>/` worktree path match; reachability-gated before OSC write |
| Also fix cross-project? | **Yes — also fix cross-project** | Scenario 2 in scope; requires spec-law change to `rq-activeChangePointer01.7` |

## What Changes

### Scenario 1: Fresh-session auto-detect from cwd

- At plugin init (`plugin/src/index.ts:437-457`), inspect `process.cwd()`.
- If cwd matches the canonical ADV worktree pattern (`~/.local/share/opencode/worktree/{projectId}/change/{changeId}/`), extract `{changeId}`.
- Run the existing `isChangeReachable` gate. If reachable, set `state.activeChange.id = {changeId}` and call `setActiveChange` to fire the OSC write.
- If cwd doesn't match or the change isn't reachable, leave the pointer null (existing behavior).
- Must NOT trigger for non-canonical paths (random `~/dev/foo` doesn't seed the pointer).

### Scenario 2: Cross-project repoint

- Modify `handleToolExecuteBefore:661-664` — when `target_path` is set AND the tool is in `activeChangeRepointTools` AND the change is reachable **in the target project**, repoint the caller's pointer to the target-project changeId.
- Modify `recordTerminalChange` (`index.ts:919-929`, `1062-1075`) — when `adv_change_close` or `adv_change_archive` succeeds for a target-project changeId that matches the caller's pointer, clear the pointer.
- Modify `recordForgetChange` similarly.
- The pointer is now a "currently-being-worked-on" cursor, regardless of which project. The OSC writes the changeId as before.
- Reachability gate must check the TARGET project's reachability, not the caller's. May require extending `isChangeReachable` to accept a target-project context.

### Spec-law change (required for Scenario 2)

`rq-activeChangePointer01.7` is modified (see Draft Spec Deltas). The new behavior: cross-project **active-work** calls repoint; cross-project **read/diagnostic** calls still don't touch the pointer (matches user's original guardrail).

## User Outcomes

- When an agent invokes a "working on the change" tool call (same-project OR cross-project), the visible zellij pane title reflects the active change ID.
- When the agent invokes a read/list/diagnostic/cleanup tool call (same-project OR cross-project), the pane title is **not** touched.
- When a fresh OpenCode session starts in a `change/<id>/` worktree, the pane title shows the change ID at startup (subject to reachability).
- When no active change exists, the pane title is preserved.
- The fix does not regress zellij-server CPU under concurrent sessions.

## Spec law impact

**Spec-law change required** — `rq-activeChangePointer01.7` (modify operation):

- **Old**: Cross-project tool calls do not touch caller's pointer.
- **New**: Cross-project **active-work** calls (tools in `activeChangeRepointTools`) repoint the caller's pointer to the target-project changeId, gated by target-project reachability. Cross-project **read/diagnostic** calls still do not touch the pointer. Terminal-clear hooks (close/archive success) clear the caller's pointer when the terminal transition is for the changeId the pointer is currently set to, regardless of which project owns it.

**No spec-law change** for `rq-titleIdentity01` (title format unchanged) or `rq-activeChangePointer01.1-.6` (pointer hygiene unchanged for same-project).

## Affected Code

| Path | Role | Touched? |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin/src/index.ts:437-457` | Plugin init — pointer init | Yes — add cwd-based rehydrate |
| `plugin/src/index.ts:576-595` | `activeChangeRepointTools` allow-list | Verify-only — must not widen |
| `plugin/src/index.ts:608-692` | `handleToolExecuteBefore` repoint hook | Yes — remove cross-project skip; add target-project reachability check |
| `plugin/src/index.ts:919-929` | `recordTerminalChange` | Yes — clear pointer on cross-project terminal transitions |
| `plugin/src/index.ts:1077-1096` | `recordForgetChange` | Yes — clear pointer on cross-project forget |
| `plugin/src/tools/_adapters.ts:532-562` | `isChangeReachable` | Possibly — extend to accept target-project context |
| `plugin/src/events/terminal.ts:170-221` | OSC writer | Verify-only — already works |
| `plugin/src/events/terminal.test.ts` | Existing tests | Extend — cwd-detect + cross-project repoint coverage |
| `plugin/src/__tests__/active-change-pointer.test.ts` | Pointer tests | Extend — `.7` scenario revision |
| `.adv/specs/advance-meta/spec.json:2865-2877` | Spec law `rq-activeChangePointer01.7` | Yes — modify text + scenario |
| `docs/specs/advance-meta.md` | Spec doc mirror | Yes — modify |

## Related Repositories

| Repo | Role | Touched? |
|---|---|---|
| `~/dev/advance` | ADV plugin source + spec store | Yes — code + spec |
| `~/toolbox` | ADR 0008 + successor criteria reference | Reference-only — no edits |

## Constraints

- **ADR 0008** — both scenario fixes are in-process state changes; no subprocess forks. Property #5 (≥16-session stress test) likely N/A; properties #6 (clean uninstall) and #7 (crash safety) apply trivially.
- **`rq-titleIdentity01`** — title format contract; active → changeId, +Epic → `epicId | changeId`, none → no write. Unchanged.
- **`rq-activeChangePointer01.1-.6`** — same-project hygiene unchanged.
- **`activeChangeRepointTools` allow-list** — must not be widened; already the correct narrow set.
- **Multi-session races** — if multiple OpenCode sessions on the same project both think they own the pointer, the OSC writes will race. Each session has its own in-process pointer; OSC writes only the local session's pane. No race at the OSC layer.
- **Cross-project reachability check** — must NOT block the tool call itself on the target project's reachability failure; only block the repoint.
- **Cwd-detection false positives** — the canonical worktree path pattern (`~/.local/share/opencode/worktree/{40-hex}/change/{changeId}/`) is precise enough to avoid false positives. Random dirs named `change/foo/` don't match.

## Impact

| Dimension | Impact |
|---|---|
| User-visible | Pane title appears for active change in fresh sessions AND cross-project workflows. |
| Performance | In-process state checks only; no hot-path cost. |
| Compatibility | Spec law `rq-activeChangePointer01.7` modified. Existing tests for `.7` will need update. |
| Tests | New coverage for cwd-detect + cross-project repoint; revised coverage for `.7` scenario. |

## Context

(Live evidence + triage findings preserved from prior version — see change history.)

Key live evidence:
- Zellij 0.44.3 honors OSC 0 for pane titles (source-confirmed).
- `zellij action list-panes --json` confirmed pane A in tab `adv` shows correct title; pane B in tab `tool` shows `Pane #1`.
- The bash tool's subshell can't open `/dev/tty` (ENXIO) — irrelevant; the plugin runs in OpenCode host process (TT=pts/1, STAT=Sl+).
- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1` doesn't affect the ADV plugin.

## Discovery Agenda (resolved)

1. **Which scenario?** → Scenario 1 (fresh session) AND Scenario 2 (cross-project) per user clarification.
2. **Scenario 1 detection mechanism?** → Auto-detect from cwd.
3. **Scenario 2 in scope?** → Yes; spec-law change to `rq-activeChangePointer01.7`.
4. **ADR 0008 applicability** — N/A for in-process state changes (no subprocess forks).

## Scope

### In Scope

- Cwd-based active-change detection at plugin init (Scenario 1).
- Cross-project repoint for `activeChangeRepointTools` (Scenario 2).
- Cross-project terminal-clear on close/archive/forget success.
- Spec-law change to `rq-activeChangePointer01.7`.
- Test coverage for both scenarios.

### Out of Scope

- TAB title changes — launcher owns those.
- Per-event status cues — broader ADR 0008 successor backlog; separate work.
- tmux code path changes — zellij focus only.
- Pointer persistence to disk file — user chose cwd-detection instead.
- Touching `zellij-project-launcher` dead code.
- Per-change "last-active timestamp" tracking for picking the most-recent change when cwd doesn't match a worktree.

### Must Not

- **Must not** reintroduce `opencode-zellij-status` server plugin.
- **Must not** widen the trigger surface beyond `activeChangeRepointTools`.
- **Must not** clear or overwrite the pane title when no active change exists (`rq-titleIdentity01.2`).
- **Must not** regress the tmux code path.
- **Must not** add a new dependency.
- **Must not** repoint on read/list/diagnostic/cleanup tool calls — including cross-project reads.
- **Must not** infer changeId from non-canonical paths (random `~/dev/foo` or `change/<id>/` in arbitrary locations).
- **Must not** block the tool call on target-project reachability failure — only block the repoint.
documents.problemStatement:
# Problem Statement

The ADV plugin already attempts to write the active change ID into the zellij pane title via OSC 0 escape sequences (`plugin/src/events/terminal.ts:170-221`), triggered by the `activeChangeRepointTools` allow-list (`plugin/src/index.ts:576-595`) — exactly the set of "actively working on the change" tool calls the user wants this for. The code is correct in intent but the OSC bytes are not reaching zellij: pane frames stay at the default `Pane #1` (zellij's fallback name when no title has been set).

## Why this matters

- The agent loses an at-a-glance visual cue of which change is active in which zellij pane. With 8+ concurrent ADV change agents in a single `main` session, this is a meaningful coordination tax.
- The trigger surface (the `activeChangeRepointTools` allow-list) is already the correct, narrow, intent-aligned set: it fires only on `adv_task_add`, `adv_task_update`, `adv_task_cancel`, `adv_task_reclassify_tdd`, `adv_task_checkpoint`, `adv_run_test`, `adv_wisdom_add`, `adv_gate_complete`, `adv_change_reenter`, `adv_change_update`, `adv_change_update_issues`, `adv_change_repair_origin`, `adv_delta_add`, `adv_delta_modify`, `adv_contract_mint`, `adv_contract_review_matrix_set`, `adv_subagent_report_submit`, `adv_ops_evidence_add` — never on reads, lists, diagnostics, cleanup, status, or repair.
- The spec law `rq-titleIdentity01` already defines the desired behavior: active change → `changeId`; + Epic → `epicId | changeId`; none → no write (preserve last title). The bug is that the spec is not realized under zellij, not that the spec is missing.

## Confirmed symptom (post-triage)

Pane frame border shows `Pane #1` — zellij's default fallback name. This rules out "OSC fires but is overwritten" and "title race lost"; it confirms the OSC write is **not reaching zellij at all**.

## Spec law impact

No spec change required. `rq-titleIdentity01` (in `.adv/specs/advance-meta/spec.json:2767-2806`) is the durable behavior contract; this change fixes the implementation to actually achieve it under zellij.

- **C6.** Multi-session safety — concurrent OpenCode sessions on the same project must not corrupt each other's in-process pointer (already true; pointers are session-local).
- **C7.** Reachability gate stays three-tier (Visibility → disk change.json → workflow state) per `rq-activeChangePointer01.5`; the cross-project path extends it to query the target project's tiers, not bypass it.
- **C8.** Spec delta is a modify operation on `rq-activeChangePointer01.7`; no new spec requirement is introduced.

## Avoidances

- **DONT1.** No `opencode-zellij-status` server plugin revival or any equivalent per-event fork storm (ADR 0008 do-not-revive).
- **DONT2.** No widening of the trigger surface beyond `activeChangeRepointTools` — including no repoint on read/list/diagnostic/cleanup/repair tool calls.
- **DONT3.** No clearing or overwriting the pane title when no active change exists (`rq-titleIdentity01.2` — preserve last intentional title).
- **DONT4.** No regression of the tmux code path.
- **DONT5.** No new third-party dependency.
- **DONT6.** No inference of changeId from non-canonical paths (random `~/dev/foo`, `~/scratch/change/bar`, etc.).
- **DONT7.** No blocking of tool execution on target-project reachability failure — only the repoint is skipped.
- **DONT8.** No per-event status cues (▶ ? ↻ ! ✓ emoji palette) — broader ADR 0008 successor backlog, separate work.
- **DONT9.** No TAB title changes — the launcher owns those with project abbreviation.

## Preview Applicability

- **visual_surface:** `true`
- **preview_expectation:**
  - `exact_route_required:` `not_applicable`
  - `data_state_expectation:` `live`
  - `viewport_expectation:` `not_applicable`
- **rationale:** The visual surface is the zellij pane frame title, not a browser-rendered UI. Verification requires a live zellij session with an OpenCode+ADV plugin instance writing OSC to the actual PTY — no preview server, no browser viewport. Browser-based preview tools (Playwright, Vite dev server) cannot reach this surface. Live verification: spawn OpenCode in a `change/<id>/` worktree inside a zellij session and inspect `zellij action list-panes --json` for the resulting pane title.

## Decisions

### User Decisions

- **UD1.** *Which scenario produces `Pane #1`?* → "Fresh session — never shows until restart." Implies Scenario 1 (fresh-session pointer rehydration) is in scope. Why it matters: confirms the fix target is plugin init, not transport.
- **UD2.** *Fresh-session detection mechanism?* → "Auto-detect from cwd (Recommended)." Implies the plugin inspects `process.cwd()` at init and infers changeId from the canonical worktree path pattern. Why it matters: avoids per-session file persistence (simpler, no multi-session races).
- **UD3.** *Cross-project scope?* → "Yes — also fix cross-project." Implies `rq-activeChangePointer01.7` spec law is modified and `handleToolExecuteBefore` no longer skips cross-project repoints for active-work tools. Why it matters: matches the user's mental model that cross-project ADV work is still active work on a change; the cue should follow the work, not the project.

### Agent Decisions (LBP)

- **AD1.** OSC transport is correct as-is (live evidence: pane in tab `adv` shows correct title). No transport change needed. Discovery disproved the original triage hypothesis of "silent TTY write failure."
- **AD2.** Cwd-detection uses the canonical worktree path pattern (`~/.local/share/opencode/worktree/{40-hex}/change/{changeId}/`), which is precise enough to avoid false positives. The pattern is anchored on `ADV_WORKTREE_HOME` and is structurally produced only by `adv_worktree_create` / `adv_worktree_resume`.
- **AD3.** Cross-project reachability requires extending `isChangeReachable` to query the target project's tiers (not the caller's). The existing three-tier order is preserved.
- **AD4.** Terminal-clear hooks (`recordTerminalChange`, `recordForgetChange`) need symmetric update: when the terminal transition is for the changeId the caller's pointer currently matches (regardless of project), clear it. The "caller project vs target project" distinction collapses — the pointer represents "the change currently being worked on."
- **AD5.** ADR 0008 successor property #5 (≥16-session stress test) is N/A: the fix introduces no subprocess forks, no IPC, no per-event work. Properties #6 and #7 apply trivially (in-process state is naturally crash-safe and leaves no orphan state if disabled).
- **AD6.** Spec delta is a single modify operation on `rq-activeChangePointer01.7`. No new spec requirement; no rename; no remove.

## Deferred Questions

None. All three Phase 4.5 questions resolved by user.

## Sign-Off

- Proposal gate completed 2026-07-21T02:33:37Z (user "approve" reply).
- Discovery open-question round 1 conducted; all 3 questions answered.
- AC checkpoint approved 2026-07-21 via user "approve" reply.
- Agreement persisted by agent post-approval per `/adv-discover` Phase 4.6 contract.

# Design

> **Phase 3.6 validator verdict: CAUTION (resolved in design).** Independent adv-researcher validation flagged that cross-project repoint using caller-scoped `resolveChangeContext` would lose target-project Epic membership, violating `rq-titleIdentity01.3` (epicId | changeId format). Design updated in KD3b + Slice B step 4 to resolve target Epic context from the target project's change.json before `setActiveChange`. Other validator findings (terminal-clear correctness ✓, spec-law delta necessity ✓, disk-only reachability viability ✓, simplicity ✓) confirmed the design's direction.

## Architecture Overview

Two surgical modifications to `plugin/src/index.ts`, plus one spec-law text revision. No new modules; no new dependencies; no subprocess forks; no IPC.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ plugin/src/index.ts (closure scope of advancePluginImpl)            │
│                                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────┐                                   │
│  │ INIT PATH (lines 437-457)    │                                   │
│  │  state.activeChange = {null} │                                   │
│  │  + cwdDetectAndRepoint() ◄───┼─── NEW: scan cwd, maybe repoint   │
│  └──────────────────────────────┘                                   │
│                                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  │ tool.execute.before hook (handleToolExecuteBefore)                │
│  │  if shouldRepointActiveChange(tool, args):                        │
│  │    if args.target_path:                                           │
│  │ -    SKIP  ◄──────────────────────────── OLD (delete this branch)│
│  │ +    targetCtx = resolveTargetProject(args.target_path)           │
│  │ +    targetDeps = buildTargetDiskDeps(targetCtx.externalRoot)     │
│  │ +    reachable = isChangeReachable(targetCtx.projectId, ...)      │
│  │ +    if reachable:                                                │
│  │ +      epicId = readTargetEpicId(targetCtx, cid) ◄── KD3b (NEW)   │
│  │ +      setActiveChange(cid, { epicId })                           │
│  │    else: ... existing same-project path                           │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│                                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  │ tool.execute.after hook (recordTerminalChange / Forget)           │
│  │  Already clears when terminal.changeId === state.activeChange     │
│  │  No changes needed — symmetric clear falls out naturally.         │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The existing OSC writer (`events/terminal.ts:170-221`), title composer (`buildTabTitle`), status mirror (`events/status.ts:132-162`), and reachability helper (`tools/_adapters.ts:532-562`) are all reused unchanged.

## Key Decisions

### KD1: Cwd-detect happens at plugin init, not on every tool call

**Decision:** `cwdDetectAndRepoint()` runs once at plugin init (after `state.activeChange = { id: null }`, around `index.ts:457`). It inspects `process.cwd()`, attempts to match the canonical worktree pattern, runs the reachability gate, and conditionally repoints.

**Rationale:**
- The user's chosen mechanism (UD2) is "auto-detect from cwd" — this is naturally a startup-time check.
- Running it per-tool-call would be wasteful (cwd rarely changes mid-session) and would broaden the trigger surface (violates DONT2).
- Subsequent same-project repoints during the session overwrite the init-time value via the existing hook — so cwd-detect is a *fallback seed*, not an authority.

**Trust model:** Agent-only. The user opts in by opening OpenCode in a worktree path; no per-call decision needed.

**Blast radius if wrong:** Low. False positive seeds the pointer to a changeId that the user isn't actually working on; the next `activeChangeRepointTools` call overwrites it. False negative just leaves the pointer null (existing behavior).

### KD2: Cwd-detect uses the canonical worktree path pattern, anchored on `getWorktreeBase(resolvedProjectId)`

**Decision:** The pattern is `${getWorktreeBase(resolvedProjectId)}/change/{changeId}/?`. `getWorktreeBase` already centralizes the `ADV_WORKTREE_HOME` override + XDG fallback logic (`utils/project-id.ts:330`).

**Rationale:**
- Reuses the existing path-computing helper — no new path logic.
- Anchoring on `resolvedProjectId` (the plugin's own project) ensures the seed matches the project the plugin loaded for, not some unrelated worktree.
- The `{changeId}` segment is extracted by splitting on `/` and taking the first non-empty path component after `/change/` — exact-match, not regex.

**Trust model:** Agent-only. Pattern is structural; no user input.

**Blast radius if wrong:** False positives possible if a non-ADV directory happens to live at `{worktreeBase}/change/{x}/`. Mitigated by the reachability gate (changeId must be a real change in the project).

### KD3: Cross-project reachability uses disk-only check on the target project's changesDir

**Decision:** For `target_path` calls, build a target-scoped `reachabilityDeps` whose `diskChecker` reads from the target project's changesDir (resolved via `resolveTargetProject` + `targetContext.externalRoot`). Skip the Visibility and workflow-state tiers for cross-project.

**Rationale:**
- The Visibility and workflow-state tiers in the existing `reachabilityDeps` (`index.ts:389-409`) use the caller's `store.changes.get(cid)`, which queries the caller's Temporal. For cross-project, we'd need to open a Temporal client to the target project — expensive and out of scope.
- The disk check (`existsSync(changesDir + "/" + cid + "/change.json")`) is sufficient: if the change.json exists in the target project's external root, the change is real.
- This honors C4 (no tool-call blocking) — the disk check is one stat, microsecond-cost.
- The spec revision (AC8) explicitly documents this disk-only check as the cross-project path.

**Trust model:** Agent-only. Mechanism choice.

**Blast radius if wrong:** Low. If the disk check false-positives (somehow a change.json exists for a non-real change), the pointer gets seeded to a phantom; the OSC write fires with a wrong title. Mitigation: change.json is only written by `adv_change_create`, so false positives require deliberate forgery.

**Alternative considered:** Resolve full target-project Temporal client and run the 3-tier check. Rejected: too expensive for a hot-path hook; the disk check is good enough for "is this changeId real in the target project".

### KD3b: Target Epic context is resolved from the target project's change.json (not the caller's store)

**Decision:** After reachability succeeds and before `setActiveChange(targetChangeId, ...)`, read the target project's change.json (`${targetContext.externalRoot}/changes/${targetChangeId}/change.json`) and extract `epic_membership.epic_id` if present. Pass it as `setActiveChange(targetChangeId, { epicId })`.

**Rationale:**
- The existing `resolveChangeContext` (index.ts:895-907) is closure-scoped to the caller's store. Calling it for a target-project changeId returns no epicId (the change doesn't exist in the caller's project).
- This violates `rq-titleIdentity01.3` — the title would be just `changeId` instead of `epicId | changeId` for cross-project Epic members.
- The fix is a single additional file read at repoint time: parse the target's change.json, extract `epic_membership?.epic_id`, pass to `setActiveChange`.

**Trust model:** Agent-only. Read-only disk I/O.

**Blast radius if wrong:** Low. If change.json parse fails or epic_membership is absent, the title falls back to bare `changeId` (acceptable per `rq-titleIdentity01.1`). If parse succeeds with stale epic data, the title shows the stale epic prefix — transient; next same-project repoint or session restart resets it.

**Validator evidence:** [index.ts:895-907](file:///home/jon/dev/advance/plugin/src/index.ts#L895-L907) confirms `resolveChangeContext` is caller-scoped; [chat-output-display spec:389-399](file:///home/jon/dev/advance/docs/specs/chat-output-display.md#L389-L399) confirms `epicId | changeId` is MUST when Epic membership exists.

### KD4: Terminal-clear hooks need NO code changes

**Decision:** Leave `recordTerminalChange` (`index.ts:919-929`) and the forget-clear path (`index.ts:1077-1096`) unchanged.

**Rationale:** The existing `recordTerminalChange` already clears when `terminal.changeId === state.activeChange.id` — agnostic to which project owns the change. Once the cross-project repoint path (KD3 + KD3b) populates the pointer with a target-project changeId, the existing terminal-clear naturally fires when the matching close/archive happens. **Validator confirmed:** [index.ts:919-929](file:///home/jon/dev/advance/plugin/src/index.ts#L919-L929) shows project-agnostic matching.

Same for `recordForgetChange`: the before-hook validates `args.changeId === state.activeChange.id` (else `FORGET_MISMATCH`); after-hook clears. Both work for cross-project changeIds once the pointer is set.

The spec text for `rq-activeChangePointer01.7` second sentence ("The terminal-clear hooks likewise do not clear the caller's pointer for target-project close/archive operations") needs to be revised to match the new behavior — but the code already does the right thing once the pointer can be set cross-project.

**Trust model:** Agent-only. Code archeology.

**Blast radius if wrong:** If I'm wrong about the existing code being agnostic, cross-project close/archive would fail to clear the pointer, leaving a stale title. Mitigation: tests (AC5) will verify.

### KD5: Spec delta is a modify operation on `rq-activeChangePointer01.7` text + scenario

**Decision:** The spec body and scenario `.7` are rewritten to reflect:
- Active-work cross-project calls (tools in `activeChangeRepointTools`) repoint the caller's pointer to the target changeId, gated by target-project disk reachability (existence of target's change.json).
- Read/diagnostic cross-project calls do NOT touch the pointer.
- Terminal-clear hooks (close/archive/forget) clear the caller's pointer when the changeId matches, regardless of project.

**Rationale:** Honors AC8 and AC9. Single modify delta; no rename, no new requirement. **Validator confirmed:** current `.7` forbids cross-project repointing; modify delta is necessary.

**Trust model:** Agent-only. Spec law codification.

**Blast radius if wrong:** Spec/implementation drift. Mitigation: tests asserting both spec text and runtime behavior.

## ADR Drafts

None. The decisions above are easily reversible (in-process state), unsurprising with the discovery context (the OSC mechanism already works), and not the result of significant tradeoffs (the alternatives were rejected for clear reasons in KD3). ADR rubric (hard-to-reverse + surprising + real-tradeoff) not satisfied.

## Implementation Strategy

Three independent slices, sequenced by risk:

### Slice A: Spec delta (lowest risk)
1. Modify `.adv/specs/advance-meta/spec.json:2865-2877` — rewrite `rq-activeChangePointer01.7` body text + scenario `then[]` array.
2. Mirror the change in `docs/specs/advance-meta.md` (corresponding rq section).
3. Update `plugin/src/__tests__/active-change-pointer.test.ts` — the `.7` scenario test must reflect new expected behavior (repoint happens for active-work tools; doesn't happen for reads).
4. Run existing test suite; verify no other `.7` consumers break.

### Slice B: Cross-project repoint path (medium risk)
1. In `handleToolExecuteBefore` (`index.ts:658-692`), replace the `if (args.target_path) { debugLog(skip) }` branch with:
   - Resolve target project context via existing `resolveTargetProject({ currentProjectPath: directory, target_path: args.target_path })` from `tools/target-project.ts:127`. Read-only resolution (no `mutation: true` needed).
   - Build a target-scoped `reachabilityDeps` with a `diskChecker` that reads `${targetContext.externalRoot}/changes/${cid}/change.json`.
   - Call `isChangeReachable(targetContext.projectId, cid, targetDeps, targetContext.changesDir)`.
2. **NEW (KD3b):** If reachable, before calling `setActiveChange`:
   - Read `${targetContext.externalRoot}/changes/${cid}/change.json` (best-effort; failures logged and treated as no-epic).
   - Parse and extract `epic_membership?.epic_id` if present.
3. Repoint + `setActiveChange(cid, { epicId })`.
4. Add unit tests in `active-change-pointer.test.ts` covering:
   - AC3 (repoint for active-work tools with target_path).
   - AC4 (no repoint for non-repoint tools with target_path).
   - AC5 (cross-project close/archive clears pointer when changeId matches).
   - AC6 (cross-project forget clears pointer when changeId matches).
   - AC7 (target reachability failure does not block tool call).
   - KD3b: title composition includes `epicId | changeId` when target change has epic_membership.
5. Verify AC7 — the existing `try/catch` in `handleToolExecuteBefore:686-690` already preserves tool-call continuation.

### Slice C: Cwd-detect at init (lowest risk after spec)
1. Add a helper `cwdDetectAndRepoint(directory, resolvedProjectId, state, store, reachabilityDeps)` near the existing init code (`index.ts:457`).
2. Implementation:
   ```ts
   const worktreeBase = getWorktreeBase(resolvedProjectId);
   const cwd = process.cwd();
   const prefix = worktreeBase + "/change/";
   if (!cwd.startsWith(prefix)) return;
   const rest = cwd.slice(prefix.length);
   const changeId = rest.split("/")[0];
   if (!changeId) return;
   try {
     const reachable = await isChangeReachable(resolvedProjectId, changeId, reachabilityDeps, store?.paths.changes ?? "");
     if (reachable) {
       state.activeChange.id = changeId;
       const ctx = await resolveChangeContext(changeId);  // same-project; existing helper works
       setActiveChange(changeId, ctx);
       debugLog(`cwdDetect: seeded pointer to ${changeId} from cwd ${cwd}`);
     }
   } catch (err) {
     debugLog(`cwdDetect: reachability check failed for ${changeId}: ${err}`);
   }
   ```
3. Note: cwd-detect is always same-project (the cwd matches the caller's worktree base), so `resolveChangeContext` works correctly here — no KD3b-style target Epic resolution needed.
4. Call it after `state` is constructed but before the existing init continuations (peer session detection, etc.). Make it best-effort: failures are logged and ignored.
5. Add unit tests covering AC1 (match → seed) and AC2 (no match → null).

### Slice ordering rationale

Spec first (Slice A) because the test changes in B and C assert against spec semantics. Then B (cross-project) because it's the higher-risk change and benefits from spec clarity; B also carries the KD3b target-Epic fix. Then C (cwd-detect) which is purely additive.

## LBP Analysis

This design is the long-term-best-practice path because:

1. **Minimal surface area.** No new modules, no new IPC, no new persistence layer. Reuses the existing `activeChangeRepointTools` allow-list, the existing reachability helper, the existing OSC writer, the existing terminal-clear hooks. The fix is "remove an over-cautious skip + add an init-time seed + add one file-read for target Epic context."

2. **No ADR 0008 regression risk.** All changes are in-process state. No subprocess forks. No per-event work. ADR 0008 was about per-event `rename-tab-by-id` fork storms; this design introduces zero forks.

3. **Falls naturally out of the spec law.** `rq-titleIdentity01` says "active change → changeId in title" (and `epicId | changeId` when Epic member). The bug was that the pointer wasn't getting set in two scenarios. The fix sets it, including the target-Epic prefix for cross-project work.

4. **Testable in isolation.** Each slice has independent tests. Cwd-detect is a pure function of `process.cwd()` + worktree base. Cross-project repoint is a function of `args.target_path` + reachability + target change.json read. Spec delta is a text change.

5. **No conflict with in-flight `fixPoisonedRecovery`.** That change touches the recovery paths inside the *tools themselves* (adv_task_update's recoveryMode handling, etc.); this change touches the `tool.execute.before` hook that runs *before* the tool. Different layers.

The alternative — persisting the pointer to a per-session file — was rejected by the user (UD2 chose cwd-detect). File persistence introduces multi-session races and cleanup complexity; cwd-detection is stateless and naturally correct.

The alternative — full target-project Temporal client for cross-project reachability — was rejected as too expensive for a hot-path hook; disk-only check is sufficient signal.

## Affected Components

| Component | File | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin init | `plugin/src/index.ts:437-457` | Add cwd-detect helper + call |
| Repoint hook | `plugin/src/index.ts:658-692` | Replace target_path skip with target-project reachability check + KD3b target Epic read |
| Spec law | `.adv/specs/advance-meta/spec.json:2865-2877` | Rewrite `.7` body + scenario |
| Spec doc mirror | `docs/specs/advance-meta.md` (corresponding rq section) | Mirror spec change |
| Pointer tests | `plugin/src/__tests__/active-change-pointer.test.ts` | Update `.7` test; add AC1-AC7 coverage + KD3b Epic-title test |

**Unchanged (verify-only):**
- `plugin/src/events/terminal.ts:170-315` (OSC writer + title composer)
- `plugin/src/events/status.ts:132-184` (status state mirror)
- `plugin/src/index.ts:576-595` (`activeChangeRepointTools` allow-list — must NOT widen per C3)
- `plugin/src/index.ts:919-929` (`recordTerminalChange` — naturally handles cross-project clear per KD4)
- `plugin/src/index.ts:1077-1096` (`recordForgetChange` — same)
- `plugin/src/tools/_adapters.ts:532-562` (`isChangeReachable` — reused)

## Design-Derived Criteria

These are technical criteria caused by the architecture; no new user-facing AC.

- **DDC1.** Cwd-detect must complete in <10ms (one `getWorktreeBase` call, one `process.cwd()` call, one `startsWith` check, optionally one `existsSync` + one `isChangeReachable` call). Must not block plugin init.
- **DDC2.** Cross-project reachability check must complete in <50ms (one `resolveTargetProject` call which does config load + `getProjectId`; one `existsSync` on the target's change.json; one additional read for change.json parse per KD3b). The existing `try/catch` already prevents tool-call blocking on failure.
- **DDC3.** The target-project disk checker must use `targetContext.externalRoot` (the canonical path), not a hand-constructed path. This ensures consistency with how other cross-project code finds the target's state.
- **DDC4.** Spec delta must be a single modify operation on `rq-activeChangePointer01.7` (per C8). No new requirement, no rename, no remove.
- **DDC5 (NEW, KD3b).** Target Epic context resolution must be best-effort: failures (file missing, parse error, no `epic_membership` field) fall through to bare `changeId` title (per `rq-titleIdentity01.1`), not error. The title composition must never throw.

## Risks / Mitigations

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cwd-detect false positive (cwd happens to match worktree pattern for a non-active change) | Low — pattern is structurally produced by `adv_worktree_create` only | Low — next `activeChangeRepointTools` call overwrites | Reachability gate (change.json must exist) + spec tests |
| Cross-project reachability check adds latency to every `target_path` repoint tool call | Medium — `resolveTargetProject` + change.json read do I/O | Low — <50ms per call, only fires for active-work tools with `target_path` | Acceptable cost; consistent with existing same-project check |
| Stale pointer after cross-project close/archive (if `extractTerminalSuccess` doesn't return changeId for target_path outputs) | Low — output format is consistent across same/cross-project | Medium — title would stay on stale changeId | AC5 test explicitly verifies cross-project archive clears pointer |
| Spec text change breaks consumers of `rq-activeChangePointer01.7` | Low — spec is internal, consumers are tests | Low — test failures caught in CI | Update tests in same slice (Slice A) |
| Concurrent OpenCode sessions in the same worktree both seed pointer to same changeId | Low — multi-session same-worktree is rare (warning emitted by existing code) | None — pointers are per-session, OSC writes only local pane | No mitigation needed; existing behavior |
| `resolveTargetProject` requires `mutation: true` for untrusted targets, complicating the hook path | Low — we pass `mutation: false` (read-only resolution); the existing API supports this | None — `mutation: false` skips the confirmation gate | Verify in implementation; test with untrusted target_path |
| **(NEW) Target change.json parse failure leaves title without Epic prefix** | Low — change.json is written atomically by `adv_change_create` | Low — title falls back to bare `changeId` (per `rq-titleIdentity01.1`) | DDC5: best-effort parse; never throw |

## Design Leverage Scout

**Scout: skipped — narrow bug fix scope, in-process state changes only, no architectural leverage surface.** Two surgical modifications + one spec text revision + one file-read addition (KD3b). Reuse of existing helpers (`getWorktreeBase`, `isChangeReachable`, `resolveTargetProject`, `setActiveChange`) is already maximal; no parallelism or simplification opportunity identified.

## Validator Result

**Phase 3.5 adv-researcher validation:** `validation.status: CAUTION` — addressed in design.

| Dimension | Validator finding | Design response |
|---|---|---|
| CORRECTNESS | Terminal-clear is project-agnostic (KD4 claim verified ✓) | Confirmed; no code change needed |
| CORRECTNESS (caution) | Caller-scoped `resolveChangeContext` loses target Epic → title missing `epicId \|` prefix (violates `rq-titleIdentity01.3`) | **Added KD3b + DDC5:** read target change.json for `epic_membership.epic_id` before `setActiveChange`; best-effort, falls back to bare `changeId` |
| SIMPLICITY | Allow-list already prevents read-tool repoints ✓; exact path-component matching preferred over regex | Confirmed; design uses exact path split, not regex |
| SPEC-LAW COMPLIANCE | Modify delta on `.7` is necessary ✓; `.1-.6` need no change ✓ | Confirmed; spec delta scoped exactly |
| KEY ALTERNATIVES | Persistence + subprocess renaming correctly rejected; init lifecycle preferred ✓ | Confirmed |

No blockers. One caution fully addressed in design before gate completion.
documents.executiveSummary:
# Executive Summary

## Outcome

Fix delivered for ADV plugin's pane-title cue in zellij: fresh OpenCode sessions and cross-project workflows now display the active change ID in the pane frame, where they previously stayed at zellij's default `Pane #1`. The approver is confirming whether this delivered work matches the agreed acceptance criteria.

## Why It Matters

The pane title is the at-a-glance visual signal for which ADV change an agent is actively working on. With 8+ concurrent OpenCode sessions in a single zellij `main` session, missing this cue creates real coordination friction. The fix removes that friction without re-introducing the ADR 0008 fork-storm pattern (no subprocess forks; purely in-process state).

## Verdict

APPROVED

## What Was Built

1. **Spec law revised** (`rq-activeChangePointer01.7`) — cross-project active-work tool calls now repoint the caller's pane-title pointer to the target change ID, while read/diagnostic calls still skip; terminal-clear (close/archive/forget) fires regardless of project.
2. **Cross-project repoint path** in `handleToolExecuteBefore` — replaces the previous target_path skip with target-project disk-only reachability check; resolves target's `epic_membership.epic_id` so the title shows `epicId | changeId` (not just `changeId`) for Epic members.
3. **Cwd-detect at plugin init** — inspects `process.cwd()` against the canonical ADV worktree path pattern; reachability-gated seed of `state.activeChange.id` so fresh sessions starting in a `change/<id>/` worktree immediately show the change ID.
